liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Music Never Stopped** (2 reviews): Reviewer likes it as set closer, noting it seemed lost mid-second set at the previous show; Reviewer enjoys it as the first-set closer [12][16]
- **Wharf Rat** (2 reviews): Reviewer treasures the jam coming out of Wharf Rat; Reviewer likes the jam leading from Wharf Rat back into Playing in the Band [14][15]
- **They Love Each Other** (1 review): Described as lyrical and superb, in an otherwise unremarkable first set [16]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Reviewer calls this the best of the three Scarlet-Fire pairings so far [12]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (1 review): Reviewer feels the Scarlet-Fire pairing is coming into its own here [15]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Reviewer found the second-set stretch from Terrapin through Playing to Wharf Rat listenable and worth saving [11]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): The jam is spooky and gets weird and tasty near the end before meandering onward [16]
- **U.S. Blues** (1 other source): Uploader lists U.S. Blues as the encore [1]

## The recordings

- **gd77-04-25.sbd.symons.15879.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 159 min; rated 3.11/5 by 18 [1]. Said about its sound: Fairly muffled soundboard with clipped highs; reviewer suspects several analog generations, though there is no tape waver; Very poor sound, like distant headphones left ten feet away, even on a good speaker system; Reasonable sound, far from the worst the reviewer has heard [6][9][15][17]
- **gd77-04-25.aud.goodbear.259.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 145 min; rated 2/5 by 4 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience tape: Jerry's guitar is clear, vocals distant, bass almost absent, and screaming fans pierce every song intro; Audience tape is good but a little trebly; reviewer suggests adding some bass [11][14]
- **gd1977-04-25.sbd.130529.MrBill.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 150 min; rated 3.5/5 by 6 [2]
- **gd1977-04-25.141903.s1.sbd.cm.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 12 songs; 88 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [4]

## Around the show

- Reviewer recalls tickets went to mailing-list Deadheads rather than the general public, but asks for correction [7]
- Electronic keyboard sounds are audible on the recording [11]
- Reviewer expected a slow burn with eight nights ahead; the first set felt pretty subdued [12]
- Widely circulated tape, but reviewer says it is not among the top five shows of 1977 [7]
- Reviewer says 1977 was a banner year and this Capitol run was not among its best [8]
- Reviewer calls it one of the few 1977 shows to skip [9]
- The 27th soundboard has better sound but lots of tuning and audience filler; this audience tape is also very good [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd77-04-25.sbd.symons.15879.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Tim Symons worked on this transfer, applying pitch adjustment; reviewer thinks he cut too much high end to reduce hiss; Poster hopes a better source surfaces someday; this is the best version they could make; Soundboard lineage is master reel to unknown generation to DAT to CDR, pitch corrected and de-clicked by Tim Symons [1][6][17]
- **gd77-04-25.aud.goodbear.259.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Teddy Goodbear; source: Audience Recording [3]
- **gd1977-04-25.sbd.130529.MrBill.flac16**: transferred by Bill Guarneri; source: Recording Info: SBD > R > C> C > C; Transfer Info: C > Nak DR2 > WAV > Sound Forge 10 > TLH > FLAC [2]
- **gd1977-04-25.141903.s1.sbd.cm.miller.flac1644**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Cassette Master (Sony TC-152SD/Maxell UD) [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by RareVinyl.com: [Grateful Dead Capitol Theatre, Passaic, NJ 4/25/77 - RSD 16 - EX US Vinyl box set](https://us.rarevinyl.com/products/grateful-dead-capitol-theatre-passaic-nj-4-25-77-rsd-16-ex-us-vinyl-box-set-r1-553449-878332) [19]
